stories.title: Spanish Hotel Operator Buys Chemists’ Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street for $95M
stories.excerpt: A 107-key hotel in Midtown has traded for roughly $95 million. Eurostars Hotel Company, a Spanish hotel chain managing more than 300 properties globally, has purchased the Chemists’ Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street from Azora, another Spanish company specializing in large-scale hotel investments, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. Eastdil Secured’s Jeffrey Davis and Scott Ellman arranged the deal for the seller, while it was unclear who repped the buyer. Eastdil declined to comment, while spokespeople for Eurostars and Azora did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The Real Deal first reported the news. It’s unclear when Azora acquired the 14-story hotel a block south of Grand Central Terminal, but the last trade recorded in property records was in 2007, when hotel chain Grupo Hotusa and Losan Hotels bought it for $77 million. Eurostars, which also owns the Eurostars Wall Street hotel at 129 Front Street in the Financial District, is a subsidiary of Grupo Hotusa, so the Midtown property is returning to its previous roots. The property was built around 1910, but not as a hotel. The building was originally the site of the historic headquarters of the Chemists’ Club, a prominent social and dining hub for leading scientists and industry pioneers. The building was later redeveloped by fortuna realty group in 1997 and opened in 2000 as the Dylan Hotel. Last year, it was again heavily redesigned and rebranded, and officially opened as the Chemists’ Club Hotel. The hotel is currently home to Benjamin Steakhouse on the ground floor and features amenities such as a lounge bar, coworking spaces and a fitness center. News of the sale comes after a slew of other hotel sales in Manhattan recently. In June, Meliá Hotels International bought the 12-story hotel at 132-142 West 27th Street in NoMad for $203 million, while Omni Lifestyle Living acquired a Marriott hotel at 21 West 37th Street in Midtown for $39.9 million, also in June. bullets: Eurostars Hotel Company acquires Chemists' Club Hotel, Midtown Manhattan, $95M

stories.summary: Spanish hotel operator Eurostars purchased the 107-key Chemists' Club Hotel at 52 East 41st Street in Midtown Manhattan for approximately $95 million from Azora. The property, a 14-story building completed around 1910 and last sold in 2007 for $77 million, is returning to the ownership structure of its previous parent, Grupo Hotusa. Eurostars, which manages over 300 properties globally, also owns the Eurostars Wall Street hotel in the Financial District.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Hotel acquisitions do not directly signal apartment demand or supply shifts, though continued capital activity in Manhattan real estate suggests ongoing investor confidence in the market.

stories.title: Skender Starts Conversion of Magnificent Mile Office Tower Into Residences
stories.excerpt: Skender has started the 500 N. Michigan Avenue adaptive reuse project, a transformative conversion of a 400,000-square-foot office tower into 320 residential units on Chicago’s Magnificent Mile. Developed by Connecticut-based Commonwealth Development Partners and designed by GREC Architects, the 24-story building will be reimagined as a residential community, with completion targeted for late 2027.Originally designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill and completed in 1968, the 304-foot-tall tower sits at the corner of N. Michigan Avenue and E. Illinois Street. The conversion will transform vacant floors 3 through 23 into 320 residential dwelling units, while a new 25th floor featuring indoor and outdoor amenity space will be constructed atop the building.The project represents one of the most significant office-to-residential conversions underway in Chicago’s downtown, part of a broader city initiative to address office vacancy and expand the supply of urban housing. “Projects like 500 N. Michigan represent exactly the kind of work Skender was built for,” says Alex Panici, vice president, Skender. “We’re proud to partner with Commonwealth Development Partners to breathe new life into this Magnificent Mile landmark and contribute to Chicago’s continued downtown transformation.” Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. bullets: Commonwealth Development Partners converting 500 N. Michigan, Chicago to 320 units; completion late 2027
24-story office tower (1968, SOM design); 400K sq ft transformed; new amenity floor added

stories.summary: Skender has begun construction on Commonwealth Development Partners' adaptive reuse project converting the 24-story, 400,000-square-foot office tower at 500 North Michigan Avenue (Chicago's Magnificent Mile) into 320 residential units, with completion targeted for late 2027. Originally designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill and completed in 1968, the conversion will transform floors 3–23 into apartments while adding a new 25th-floor amenity level. GREC Architects designed the residential reimagining.
stories.impact: Chicago's tight multifamily supply and strong rent growth make office-to-residential conversion economically feasible and accelerate unit delivery in a supply-constrained submarket. Large-format conversions on prime retail locations (Mag Mile) indicate landlords prefer residential revenue over stabilized office tenancy, signaling sustained apartment demand and potential for higher rents to justify conversion capex.

stories.title: Izo Capital Lends $26M on Wyoming Apartments Near Jackson Hole
stories.excerpt: Sundance Properties has sealed $25.6 million of construction financing to bring a multifamily development in Alpine, Wyo., across the finish line, Commercial Observer has learned. Izo Capital supplied the 24-month senior construction loan to fund the completion of Phase 1 of the developer’s planned the Flats at Alpine Junction project comprising 64 units. The debt will support the completion of three additional buildings comprising 48 apartments on top of 16 units that are already completed and leased. Peter Porraro, co-founder and chief investment officer at Izo Capital, said the overall project, which will eventually total 160 units, is set up for success given that it’s 35 miles from Jackson Hole mountain valley, with a number of employers based in the town of Jackson, Wyo. Porraro noted that Alpine also has demand drivers for multifamily with limited supply coupled with a newly opened medical center and a public charter school scheduled to open for the 2026-2027 academic year. “It’s very hard to develop out there, and it’s hard to get the infrastructure,” Porraro told CO of the need for more apartments projects near Jackson Hole. “There’s just no supply and nothing new in the market.” The Flats development has already shown strong leasing momentum, according to Porraro, with the current rental rates helping support underwriting assumptions in the loan for the remaining phases of the project. The first phase is slated for completion next spring. Porraro noted that there is large-scale demand for rental housing for those who work in Jackson Hole given that median home prices in the city are close to $3 million, with townhomes starting at around $1 million. He said the project at 303 Highway also benefits from transportation connectivity that includes direct access to the START Bus system linking Alpine and Jackson. “The demand we’ve experienced from the first completed building reinforces the critical need for new rental housing in Alpine,”
bullets: Izo Capital funds $25.6M construction loan to Sundance Properties, Alpine, Wyo., 64 units Phase 1
Flats at Alpine Junction; 160 units total; 35 miles Jackson Hole; 16 units completed, 48 under construction
Jackson employer base + new medical center + charter school drive demand in supply-constrained mountain market
stories.summary: Izo Capital closed a $25.6 million 24-month senior construction loan to Sundance Properties for Phase 1 of the Flats at Alpine Junction in Alpine, Wyoming, comprising 64 units (16 completed and leased, 48 under construction). The overall project will total 160 units. Alpine, located 35 miles from Jackson Hole, benefits from demand drivers including an employer base in Jackson, a newly opened medical center, and a public charter school scheduled to open for the 2026–2027 academic year, all within a supply-constrained market.
stories.impact: Jackson Hole / Alpine corridor exhibits strong multifamily demand catalysts (employer concentration, amenity buildout) coupled with development-constrained supply and financing availability. The market signals opportunity for developers to acquire sites and move forward on entitled projects ahead of further population influx; construction lending appetite suggests investor confidence in mountain-market fundamentals despite geographic constraints.

stories.title: Amkor Could Add to $7B Peoria Facility
stories.excerpt: Amkor Technology is building a $7 billion packaging and testing facility in Peoria, slated to open in 2027. Last October, Amkor broke ground on its Peoria manufacturing facility and announced it would increase its investment in the project from $2 billion to $7 billion. The Phoenix Business Journal reports Amkor’s Peoria facility has already landed backing by major customer commitments from Apple, Nvidia and a 10-year agreement with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. The company is building its 2.3 million-square-foot manufacturing campus in two phases, which will offer more than 750,000 square feet of cleanroom space and generate 3,000 new jobs. Amkor recently bought 67 acres near its advanced packaging and test facility to support potential future expansion. The post Amkor Could Add to $7B Peoria Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Amkor Technology expanding Peoria, Ariz. fab to $7B total; 2.3M sq ft; 3,000 jobs; opens 2027
Commitments from Apple, Nvidia, TSMC; recently bought 67 acres for future expansion
Major employer expansion driving job growth and in-migration to Phoenix submarket
stories.summary: Amkor Technology is expanding its Peoria, Arizona advanced packaging and test facility investment from $2 billion to $7 billion, with opening slated for 2027. The 2.3 million-square-foot manufacturing campus will generate 3,000 new jobs and includes 750,000+ square feet of cleanroom space. The company has secured customer commitments from Apple, Nvidia, and a 10-year agreement with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., and recently acquired 67 additional acres to support future expansion.
stories.impact: Amkor's significant capex and 3,000-job creation in the Peoria metro will drive strong in-migration and job-growth demand for multifamily housing in Phoenix's West Valley and Peoria submarkets over 2025–2027. Developers should prioritize land acquisition and entitlements in job-proximate locations; the 10-year TSMC agreement suggests sustained employment and rental demand beyond the facility opening.

stories.title: CW Realty Closes Deal to Buy 55 Smith Street in Downtown Brooklyn for $58M
stories.excerpt: CW Realty Group closed on a deal to acquire a parking facility in Downtown Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. Cheskie Weisz’ CW Realty entered into a contract to purchase 55 Smith Street in December from New Jersey-based firm Edison Properties, Crain’s New York Business reported at the time. The sale closed on Friday and its price was disclosed at $58 million, according to broker JLL. CW Realty has not disclosed any specifics about their plans for the site, which has an alternative address of 160 Livingston Street, but the lot spans 13,707 square feet and is one of the biggest residential development opportunities in Downtown Brooklyn, the JLL Capital Markets team said. “This transaction demonstrates the strength of demand for well-located development opportunities across New York City, particularly in neighborhoods with strong residential fundamentals and supportive zoning,” JLL’s Mike Mazzara, who negotiated the deal alongside Ethan Stanton, Brendan Maddigan and Drew Isaacson, said in a statement. “The site offers a combination of scale, flexibility and development incentives in one of Brooklyn’s most dynamic neighborhoods.” CW Realty and Edison Properties did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Developers can build 137,000 square feet on the site as of right or 164,000 square feet under the Universal Affordability Preference program with no height limits or parking requirements for a potential housing development. CW Realty has the option to build using the city’s 485-x program and benefit from reforms made under the City of Yes for Housing Opportunity. An added bonus is that development on the site is not restricted to rental housing or condominiums, according to JLL. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CW Realty acquires parking facility 55 Smith Street, Downtown Brooklyn, $58M; closed Friday
13,707 sq ft lot; one of largest residential development opportunities in area; developer plans undisclosed
Strong demand for well-located development sites; supportive zoning signals residential conversion potential
stories.summary: CW Realty Group closed acquisition of 55 Smith Street (alternative address 160 Livingston Street) in Downtown Brooklyn for $58 million, a parking facility on 13,707 square feet of land. The deal, originally contracted in December with New Jersey-based Edison Properties, represents one of Downtown Brooklyn's largest residential development opportunities. CW Realty has not disclosed specific redevelopment plans, but broker JLL highlighted the site's scale, flexibility, and supportive zoning for residential development.
stories.impact: Downtown Brooklyn's strong residential fundamentals and supportive zoning continue to attract capital for large-scale development sites; the parking-to-residential conversion opportunity and $58M price point signal investors' confidence in the submarket's demand and ability to justify construction capex. Developers competing for similar Downtown Brooklyn sites should expect continued price pressure and should accelerate entitlements and financing on owned or optioned parcels.

stories.title: Kimco Buys Two Broward Retail Centers for $109M
stories.excerpt: Kimco Realty, one of the biggest owners of grocery-anchored retail centers in the country, has acquired two more in Broward County for a combined $109 million from KPR Centers, property records show. In the largest transaction, the Jericho, N.Y.-based REIT paid $56 million for Sunshine Plaza, a 245,744-square-foot property between 4017 and 4299 West Commercial Boulevard in Tamarac, just east of the Florida’s Turnpike. Publix and Marshalls anchor the 19-acre shopping center. Other tenants include Crunch Fitness, Krispy Kreme and Subway. New York-based KPR had purchased the property for $28.5 million in 2014. In the smaller trade, Kimco Realty paid $53 million for the 254,749-square-foot Pompano Marketplace at 1115 and 1117 South Federal Highway. It also spans about 19 acres, with a Walmart Neighborhood Market as the anchor. Other tenants include Ross Dress for Less, Carrabba’s Italian Grill and TD Bank. KPR Centers had purchased the asset for $46.8 million in 2015. Kimco Realty owns 589 properties nationwide, including 44 across South Florida. In one of South Florida’s largest retail deals in recent years, the REIT paid $216 million for The Shops at Mary Brickell Village in Miami in 2022. Representatives for Kimco Realty and KPR Centers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Kimco Realty acquires two Broward County retail centers for $109M; Publix and Walmart anchors
Sunshine Plaza (Tamarac): $56M, 245K sq ft, 19 acres; Pompano Marketplace: $53M, 254K sq ft, 19 acres
Grocery-anchored retail REITs consolidating; minimal direct multifamily signal
stories.summary: Kimco Realty, a major national owner of grocery-anchored retail centers, acquired two Broward County properties for a combined $109 million. Sunshine Plaza in Tamarac (245,744 sq ft, 19 acres, anchored by Publix and Marshalls) sold for $56 million, while Pompano Marketplace (254,749 sq ft, 19 acres, anchored by Walmart Neighborhood Market) sold for $53 million. Kimco acquired both from KPR Centers, which had purchased them in 2014 and 2015, respectively, for a combined $75.3 million.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Retail REIT consolidation activity does not signal apartment supply or demand shifts, though South Florida's continued real estate transaction velocity indicates capital availability and market confidence.

stories.title: Arizona Tradeport Hubs Receive $16M Federal Grant
stories.excerpt: The plan is to streamline cargo movement and transform domestic supply chains across the country, initially stretching from California to Arizona and all the way to the East Coast. The so-called tradeport hubs project, which will be rolled out in multiple phases, intends to integrate a web of highways, train tracks and airlines within manufacturing hot spots across the U.S. The Phoenix Business Journal reports that the latest $16 million infusion of government funds will go toward developing the first three tradeport hubs, each ranging from 1,000 to 5,000 acres along the I-40 corridor. The first route is planned to connect the Port of Los Angeles to Albuquerque, New Mexico and to the BNSF Southern Transcon Railroad through northern Arizona. The two key tradeport hubs identified in Arizona are in Kingman and Winslow. An initial estimate of the total development costs for the hub in Winslow is pegged at $750 million. Global Logistics Development Partners is spearheading the effort in Arizona. The post Arizona Tradeport Hubs Receive $16M Federal Grant appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Arizona tradeport hubs receive $16M federal grant; I-40 corridor Kingman, Winslow hubs planned
1,000–5,000 acre logistics hubs; Winslow development cost estimated $750M; LA-to-East Coast supply chain integration
Long-term infrastructure and logistics employment growth in rural Arizona markets
stories.summary: Arizona's tradeport hubs project received a $16 million federal grant to develop the first three hubs (each 1,000–5,000 acres) along the I-40 corridor. Global Logistics Development Partners is spearheading the multi-phase initiative, which aims to streamline cargo movement and integrate highways, railways, and airlines across manufacturing hubs from California to the East Coast. The first route will connect the Port of Los Angeles through northern Arizona (Kingman and Winslow) to Albuquerque and the BNSF Southern Transcon Railroad; Winslow's hub alone carries an estimated $750 million development cost.
stories.impact: Long-term infrastructure investment in rural Arizona logistics corridors will eventually drive secondary-market multifamily demand in Kingman and Winslow as employment hubs mature; however, development timelines are measured in years and demand is speculative. Developers should monitor hub progress but prioritize acquisition and zoning only in Winslow (the larger hub) if clear pre-leasing or employer commitments materialize.

stories.title: OHT Breaks Ground on 360-Unit Houston Rental Community
stories.excerpt: OHT Partners has begun construction of a 360-unit apartment complex called Park Row at 14192 Park Row Blvd. in Houston. OHT recently broke ground on another project, 5 miles to the west on Park Row Boulevard. Dubbed Park Row, it will have 11 three-story buildings, a clubhouse, a pet spa and a bike storage facility on 13.7 acres. The one- and two-bedroom units will range from 702 to 1,257 square feet. Community amenities include a fitness room, coworking areas with private offices, a kitchen, package lockers, a resort-style pool with cabanas, a dog park and wash, a pickleball court, detached garages, electric vehicle chargers and outdoor grills. Meeks + Partners is the architect for the project, and OHT serves as its own general contractor. OHT anticipates starting pre-leasing in the second quarter of next year and complete the complex in the second quarter of 2028. The rental rate will be determined around the time pre-leasing begins. The company acquired the property last February. The 13.7-acre project will include 11 three-story buildings, a clubhouse, pet amenities, and resort-style finishes. Units will range from 702 to 1,257 square feet (one and two bedrooms). Pre-leasing is scheduled for Q2 2025, with completion targeted for Q2 2028. Meeks + Partners designed the project; OHT serves as general contractor.
stories.impact: Houston's continued multifamily development pipeline (360 units in a single project) reflects sustained rental demand and financing appetite in the market. Developers should monitor absorption of existing supply in the Park Row Boulevard corridor and comparable Houston submarkets; sustained pre-leasing velocity and rent achievement will validate continued Houston development feasibility and justify additional starts.

stories.title: AvalonBay, Equity Residential Will Operate as Vivmark Post-Merger
stories.excerpt: AvalonBay Communities, Inc. and Equity Residential announced Vivmark Residential as the name for the combined company resulting from their merger of equals. The new company, which expects to trade under the ticker symbol VMRK, will have a pro forma equity market capitalization of approximately $53 billion and an enterprise value of approximately $71 billion, with more than 180,000 rental apartments and over 10,000 apartments under construction. “The name Vivmark Residential reflects what we are building — a company determined to set a new standard for the experience of home,” said Benjamin Schall, CEO of AvalonBay and incoming CEO of Vivmark..”Vivmark Residential is built from the exceptional foundations that AvalonBay and Equity Residential have each spent more than 30 years establishing as trusted leaders. With the combined scale, capabilities, and talent of both organizations, we have a rare opportunity to redefine what rental housing can be.” The combined company will operate as Vivmark Residential upon completion of the merger. The new company name will not result in community name changes at closing. It’s not yet clear where the combined company will be headquartered. Where the apartment industry connects. bullets: AvalonBay, Equity Residential merge; combined company Vivmark Residential, $53B market cap, 180K+ units

stories.summary: AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential announced Vivmark Residential as the name for the combined company resulting from their merger of equals. The new company will have a pro forma equity market capitalization of approximately $53 billion, an enterprise value of approximately $71 billion, more than 180,000 rental apartments, and over 10,000 apartments under construction. The merged entity will trade under ticker VMRK, with Benjamin Schall (AvalonBay CEO) as incoming CEO. The headquarters location has not yet been determined, and individual community names will not change at closing.
stories.impact: The AvalonBay–Equity Residential merger creates the industry's largest multifamily REIT and signals potential portfolio optimization (dispositions of non-core or overlap assets), accelerated capital deployment into high-growth markets, and operational synergies that may reshape competitive dynamics. Developers should expect increased institutional competition for land and development partnerships; monitor Vivmark's early portfolio moves and capital allocation to identify divested markets where acquisition opportunities may arise and growth corridors where competition will intensify.

stories.title: Schuckman Buys Northeast Queens Shopping Center for $56M
stories.excerpt: Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center in Queens for $56 million. BTF Capital Fund, led by Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky, purchased the Key Food-anchored property at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway, according to a deed transfer in property records filed Friday. The purchase could be a play for assets tied to grocery stores and other necessity-based retail. Schuckman’s brokerage firm, Schuckman Realty, will handle leasing for the shopping center, according to the buyer. Acadia Realty Trust provided about $48.5 million in financing to Schuckman for the acquisition through a shell corporation, with Acadia’s Chief Financial Officer John Gottfried signing the mortgage documents. Punia & Marx and Acadia did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Punia & Marx has owned the property since at least 1975, and the amount paid for that acquisition is unknown. Schuckman seems to have been involved in the management operations of the 220,000-square-foot shopping center, which is also leased to a Chase Bank branch, with a 2020 flier listing Kenneth Schuckman and Jessica Vilmenay as exclusive brokers. The advertisement said at the time that a redevelopment of the property would be taking place, but was not specific about the nature of the repositioning. Schuckman promoted the center based on 100,000 cars passing by the center daily on the Cross Island Parkway and 333,000 people living within three miles. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BTF Capital Fund (Schuckman, Malinsky) acquires Whitestone Shopping Center, Queens, $56M; Key Food anchor
220K sq ft center; 153-15 Cross Island Parkway; Acadia Realty Trust provided $48.5M financing
Necessity-anchored retail consolidation; limited multifamily signal unless conversion planned
stories.summary: BTF Capital Fund, led by Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky, purchased the Whitestone Shopping Center in Queens (153-15 Cross Island Parkway) for $56 million. The 220,000-square-foot property is anchored by Key Food and includes a Chase branch. Acadia Realty Trust provided approximately $48.5 million in financing for the acquisition. Schuckman's brokerage will handle leasing for the center. The property has been held by Punia & Marx since at least 1975.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Grocery-anchored retail consolidation does not signal apartment demand or supply shifts. Monitor only if Schuckman signals conversion or mixed-use redevelopment plans for the Cross Island Parkway site; otherwise, activity reflects retail REIT and necessity-retail investor positioning in Queens.
